parameters.quote: Manufacturers must report any battery-related fire, thermal runaway, injury, evacuation, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported within 5 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 5 business days of learning of a serious incident involving their model, and promptly provide safety instructions.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report any battery-related fire, thermal runaway, injury, evacuation, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported within 5 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 5 business days of learning of a serious incident involving their model, and promptly provide safety instructions.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report any battery-related fire, thermal runaway, injury, evacuation, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported within 5 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 5 business days of learning of a serious incident involving their model, and promptly provide safety instructions. Reports must include the model, incident date, known consequences, and any immediate precautions; submit updates as facts are confirmed.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: A model with a failure rate above 5% must promptly submit a regulator-approved corrective-action plan, including interim risk controls and a retest schedule. The regulator may restrict or suspend sales if the evidence indicates an unacceptable risk or the manufacturer fails to meet the plan; exceeding 5% alone does not automatically require a sales ban.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-accepted protocol and representative production units. Manufacturers must provide per-model test methods, sample sizes, and results to the relevant regulator and retain them for audit. Customers must receive the per-model failure rate and compliance status at purchase and after any material safety update. Per-model failure rates must not be published to the general public; this does not limit disclosure to regulators or customers as provided in this section. A model with a failure rate above 5% must promptly submit a regulator-approved corrective-action plan, including interim risk controls and a retest schedule. The regulator may restrict or suspend sales if the evidence indicates an unacceptable risk or the manufacturer fails to meet the plan; exceeding 5% alone does not automatically require a sales ban.

parameters.quote: For systems already installed, manufacturers must provide a retrofit or equivalent upgrade plan and complete implementation within 6 years of this standard taking effect. Where remote shut-off is not yet available, manufacturers must provide customers with interim emergency guidance.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: For systems already installed, manufacturers must provide a retrofit or equivalent upgrade plan and complete implementation within 6 years of this standard taking effect. Where remote shut-off is not yet available, manufacturers must provide customers with interim emergency guidance.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: Newly installed systems must support a secure remote emergency shut-off capability, with clear customer instructions and safeguards against unauthorized activation. For systems already installed, manufacturers must provide a retrofit or equivalent upgrade plan and complete implementation within 6 years of this standard taking effect. Where remote shut-off is not yet available, manufacturers must provide customers with interim emergency guidance.

parameters.quote: New battery systems manufactured for sale must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard takes effect.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New battery systems manufactured for sale must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard takes effect.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New battery systems manufactured for sale must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard takes effect. The suppression system must be designed and validated for the battery’s chemistry and enclosure, and maintained according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Manufacturers must provide customers with instructions on its operation and limitations.

parameters.quote: When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and provide the underlying model-specific data and a corrective-action plan. The regulator must promptly investigate and determine appropriate protective measures, including recall where warranted by verified incident data, severity, trends, exposure, and corrective actions.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and provide the underlying model-specific data and a corrective-action plan. The regulator must promptly investigate and determine appropriate protective measures, including recall where warranted by verified incident data, severity, trends, exposure, and corrective actions.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: At purchase and after any material safety update, customers must receive the model’s thermal-test compliance status and per-model 55 °C test failure rate, relevant safety instructions, and a clear way to report incidents. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of newly identified material risks and provide protective steps. When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and provide the underlying model-specific data and a corrective-action plan. The regulator must promptly investigate and determine appropriate protective measures, including recall where warranted by verified incident data, severity, trends, exposure, and corrective actions. Regulators retain authority to require a recall below this rate where evidence warrants it.

ground_truth_claims.message_text: Northwind’s company-wide thermal-incident rate was 8.6 per 100,000 installed units last year; Hearth 10’s rate was 6.4 per 100,000. The company-wide figure is not a per-model rate, so it should not by itself trigger a model-specific recall. Hearth 10 is below the discussed 8-per-100,000 model trigger, though regulators should retain authority to act on other evidence or serious risks.

The figures shared by our drafter are the evidence we have for this proposal: Northwind’s company-wide rate was 8.6 per 100,000, while Hearth 10’s model-specific rate was 6.4. The aggregate rate does not establish that any particular model exceeds 8; a trigger tied to each model’s installed-unit rate is more targeted and actionable. We can support a mandatory recall when a model exceeds 8 per 100,000 in a 12-month period, alongside regulator authority to act sooner where severity or other evidence warrants.

ground_truth_claims.message_text: For comparison, Halcyon’s company-wide thermal-incident rate was 8.1 per 100,000 installed units last year, and our Ember 8 model-specific rate was 9.9 per 100,000. Ember 8’s 55 °C sustained-heat test failure rate was 3.9%. These figures support distinguishing incident-rate recall criteria from the separate thermal-test benchmark; they do not support withholding model-specific results or exempting a model from a consistently applied trigger.

judge_section_notes: The 5% figure in S2 is a corrective-action benchmark rather than a hard maximum, and exceeding it never automatically requires a sales stop, which protects the Hearth 10 (6.2%). In S5, the 8-per-100,000 trigger requires notification and a corrective-action plan but makes recall discretionary and open-ended, so a model at 9.9 (Ember 8) is not automatically recalled. S3's 6-year retrofit window and S4's 36-month suppression deadline both sit inside the acceptable ranges, with S4 at the earliest date Halcyon's red line allowed.
